chapter_title: What is Virginal; or, otherwise, what is Continent?
chapter_note: The chapter is built as a five-step definitional ladder (“virginal” vs “continent”) mostly in a systematic cosmological/soteriological register. The opening Q&A is hagiographic frame. The final two steps drift into community-institutional categories (“elect”) and then human sexual practice; these are later applications layered onto the underlying degree-structure teaching.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic scene-setting (“the apostle… among the congregation of his church”) and direct-address questions; this is compiling-community frame, not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Formal disciple request (“Proclaim to us, my master… good gifts… through you”): classic dialogue frame that wraps teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: What is called ‘virginal’ is assigned to the mystery of the aeons of greatness. And they called it ‘virginal’ by the category of all the light that did not [taste] of death, nor come to the enemy’s war.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“Then speaks our enlightener to them:”) as compiling-frame speech marker.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core definitional mapping (term → cosmic domain/state of Light) in an impersonal, structural voice; only the introductory speech formula is later frame.

paragraphs.core_text: However, what is called ‘continent’ occurs to the mystery of the light that came and was mixed with the darkness. It was defiled in bodies [ ... ] and went up to the light. [They] called [it ‘co]ntinent’.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos definition: Light-in-mixture vs Light’s ascent; no institutional audience address or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, the holy vir[gin]als [ ... ... ] should they come out against the en[emy ... ... not] taste death, nor [ ... ].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Lacunose, but continues the same “virginal” category as a cosmic class that does not ‘taste death’; no explicit turn to church practice, though the fragment is uncertain.

paragraphs.core_text: On the other hand, what is called ‘continent’ [is this li]ght that mixed with the darkness, was purif[ie]d, came [up f]rom all the creatures, and was confirmed in the great[ness]. They called it ‘continent’ since it tasted [of the l]ust; but afterwards was cleansed from it and [become an] holy one.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic process-description of purification and confirmation in greatness; “lust” functions as a mixture-condition within the cosmology, not as a community exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, what is called [‘vi]rginal’ is this light that was purified by the ima[ge] of the [A]mbassador. It wen[t up and] attained [the] he[ights. It was] confirmed in the image of the gods.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological mechanism anchored in named beings (Ambassador) and image/confirmation language; remains fully inside the system (no institutional targets).

paragraphs.core_text: Again, what is [called] ‘continent’ is the remainder of this light th[at] remained behind, from what was cleansed. It goes up and comes down in transmigration. Al[so], there is a part [of] it that shall come and attain the form of [hum]an [fl]esh. Again, that one too shall be chosen in the flesh, [accept] the hope, and become an holy one. And they name it ‘continent’.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree-step description of remaining Light and transmigration into flesh; still explanatory (how the Light moves/stabilizes), not hortatory.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, what is named ‘virginal’ is the Light Mind. However, on the other hand, what is called ‘contin[ent]’ is the new man, should it be purified from this old man. And it is cleansed and strips off the sin that is compounded with it, and it becomes a continent one.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the clause “should he come and assume the images [of] the ele[ct]” because it maps a cosmic entity onto a contemporary institutional category (“elect”), crossing from cosmos→cosmos into cosmos→community application.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying core mapping (Virginal/Continent → Light Mind/new man) is degree-structured, but the ‘elect’ identification is a later institutional graft; ‘old man/new man’ also echoes later Christian idiom, reinforcing mixed layering.
Directly about human sexual status and renunciation “in the flesh” (man/woman/intercourse); this is behavioral-ascetic application rather than cosmological architecture.
Meta-concluding speaker remark (“I have taught you… in many forms”) functioning as closure rather than continuing the systematic cosmological mappings.
